create_circuits.ponder.and.header: Combining signals with the AND gate
create_circuits.ponder.and.text_1: The AND gate combines two redstone inputs into a single output
create_circuits.ponder.and.text_2: One input alone is not enough, the gate stays dark
create_circuits.ponder.and.text_3: With both inputs powered the gate fires and lights up the lamp
create_circuits.ponder.and.text_4: Cut a single input and the output goes quiet again
create_circuits.ponder.nand.header: Inverting AND with the NAND gate
create_circuits.ponder.nand.text_1: The NAND gate inverts AND: it stays lit while at least one input is missing
create_circuits.ponder.nand.text_2: One powered input alone is not enough to flip the output
create_circuits.ponder.nand.text_3: Only when both inputs are powered does the gate fall silent and the lamp go dark
create_circuits.ponder.nand.text_4: Drop a single input and the inverted output lights up again
create_circuits.ponder.nor.header: Inverting OR with the NOR gate
create_circuits.ponder.nor.text_1: The NOR gate fires only when neither input is powered
create_circuits.ponder.nor.text_2: A single powered input is enough to silence the output
create_circuits.ponder.nor.text_3: Powering the second input keeps the output dark
create_circuits.ponder.nor.text_4: Cut both inputs and the gate fires again
create_circuits.ponder.not.header: Inverting a signal with the NOT gate
create_circuits.ponder.not.text_1: The NOT gate flips its only input: idle in means powered out
create_circuits.ponder.not.text_2: Power the input and the output drops, leaving the lamp dark
create_circuits.ponder.not.text_3: Cut the input again and the gate lights the lamp back up
create_circuits.ponder.or.header: Combining signals with the OR gate
create_circuits.ponder.or.text_1: The OR gate fires whenever at least one input is powered
create_circuits.ponder.or.text_2: Powering a single input is already enough to light the lamp
create_circuits.ponder.or.text_3: Powering both inputs keeps the output high
create_circuits.ponder.or.text_4: Only when every input drops does the gate fall silent
create_circuits.ponder.subtractor.text_1: The Subtractor returns the first input minus the second, clamped at zero
create_circuits.ponder.subtractor.text_2: Set the first input to 15 and nothing on the second: the full signal passes
create_circuits.ponder.subtractor.text_3: Raise the second input to 7 and the output drops to 15 minus 7, or 8
create_circuits.ponder.subtractor.text_4: Match the two inputs and the output is exactly zero
create_circuits.ponder.subtractor.text_5: If the second input is larger, the result is clamped at zero rather than going negative
create_circuits.ponder.xnor.header: Matching signals with the XNOR gate
create_circuits.ponder.xnor.text_1: The XNOR gate inverts XOR and fires whenever the two inputs agree
create_circuits.ponder.xnor.text_2: Powering a single input breaks the match and the lamp goes dark
create_circuits.ponder.xnor.text_3: Powering the other input restores the match and the lamp lights up
create_circuits.ponder.xnor.text_4: Disagree once more and the gate falls silent
create_circuits.ponder.xor.header: Comparing signals with the XOR gate
create_circuits.ponder.xor.text_1: The XOR gate fires only when its two inputs disagree
create_circuits.ponder.xor.text_2: Powering a single input drives the output high
create_circuits.ponder.xor.text_3: Matching inputs cancel out and the gate falls silent again
create_circuits.ponder.xor.text_4: Break the symmetry by dropping one input and the lamp lights again
